name: Cryptosporidium spp.

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Oocyst: round, approximately 4–6 µm, containing four sporozoites without sporocysts.
Modified acid-fast appearance varies from pink-red to unstained; species cannot be separated by oocyst morphology.

transmission.detail: Infective oocysts contaminate water, food or hands. Intestinal replication includes stages capable of maintaining autoinfection.

life_cycle.detail: Infective oocysts contaminate water, food or hands. Intestinal replication includes stages capable of maintaining autoinfection.

hosts: Humans and many animals depending on species; C. hominis and C. parvum are prominent human pathogens. No intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide, including Southeast Asia; waterborne and zoonotic exposures matter.
clinical_significance: Watery diarrhea; prolonged severe illness is particularly important in immunocompromised patients and young children.
diagnostics: Modified acid-fast stains at 400–1000×, fluorescent antibody methods, antigen assays or molecular testing.
Record preparation and calibrated size; ordinary wet mounts can miss these small organisms.
differential_diagnosis: Cyclospora is larger at roughly 8–10 µm; yeast and precipitate can mimic small round objects. A red dot alone is insufficient evidence.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Cryptosporidium spp. — Cryptosporidium coccidia. Watery diarrhea; prolonged severe illness is particularly important in immunocompromised patients and young children.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
